  - constants: `OFFICE_LOCK_PREFIX` = '~$', `PDF_EXTENSION` = 'pdf'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/page.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - enforces: `rule:no-AI-on-client-documents`
  - tested by: `tests/test_validators.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Never downloads a cloud-only placeholder — a stub must never be filed as if it were the document. A file that vanishes between listing and stat is reported pending_sync, never raised — a scheduled scan must not die on one replaced file. PdfVerdictCache is a run's memo of PDF readability (the router asks once per manifest row for one file; the scanner asks again): the filer and the scanner each make one and pass it down, so nothing is shared at module level between runs that might one day be concurrent. UNFINISHED_SUFFIXES is the one list of transfer-in-progress names (decision 56).
- **`tracker/view.py`** — The page a person opens: VIEW_FILENAME, regenerated in the engagement folder at the end of every real pass from the readers (load_manifest() for the request rows and their statuses, read_index() for the originals, review.triage() for what each parked file might be), in four sections - Summary, Requests, Index, Needs Review. Owns the file name, the Summary's labels and their meta names, the three words a view's state is said in (CURRENT / BEHIND / UNKNOWN), the chip's label and the button's, render_page(), write_view(), view_state(), read_stamp(), the two row builders (request_row(), index_row()) and the CLI that redraws one engagement and prints its state.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.view`
  - constants: `VIEW_FILENAME` = 'Status Report.html', `SUMMARY_SECTION` = 'Summary', `REQUESTS_SECTION` = 'Requests', `VIEW_NOTE` = 'This page is regenerated every pass and holds no facts of its own: every value on it comes from the record, the request list and the index.', `LABEL_ENGAGEMENT` = 'Engagement folder', `LABEL_GENERATED` = 'Generated (UTC)', `LABEL_GENERATED_LOCAL` = 'Generated (this machine)', `LABEL_RECORD_DIGEST` = 'Record SHA-256', `LABEL_REQUEST_ROWS` = 'Request rows', `LABEL_INDEX_ROWS` = 'Index rows', `LABEL_PARKED_ROWS` = 'Parked for a person', `VIEW_LABEL` = 'Status report', `VIEW_OPEN_LABEL` = 'Open Status Report', `NEEDS_REVIEW_FIELDS` = ('received', 'original_name', 'pbc_location', 'reason', 'candidates', 'evidence'), `BADGE_CLASS` = 'badge', `NOT_APPLICABLE_CLASS` = 'not-applicable', `NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION` = '{label} ({n})'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/page.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/review.py`
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
  - writes: `artifact:Status Report.html`
  - reads: `artifact:Status Report.html`, `artifact:_ledger.jsonl`, `artifact:tracker.db`
  - follows: `tracker/reminder.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_view.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Decision 89, stage A step 3, as decision 91 settled it: the owner's rule is that every file staff open only to READ is a web page. IT HOLDS NO FACT, and that is the whole design: no fact is read back - only the stamp in its meta tags, by read_stamp(), for the current / behind / unknown chip - so the one failure every other file must survive costs nothing here. A page whose replace does not land is not replaced, the run carries view_stale and SUCCEEDS, the older page stands and the next pass lands one. Written through manifest.write_text_atomically(); there is no read-only attribute (a browser holds no write lock). On Windows a plain open() read handle still refuses the replace, so view_stale has a real trigger there. Every value goes through page.esc() and the page fetches nothing. The stamp lives in meta tags in the head and read_stamp() reads it with one regular expression - no HTML parser in production. Decision 104: view_state() compares ONE digest - the record's head (ledger.head()) as it was when the page was drawn, against the head now; a rules edit is an event, so an edit moves the head and the page is honestly behind, and the workbook's digest that used to be the second stamp is gone with the workbook. Section headings come from their owners (REQUESTS_SECTION here, filer.INDEX_HEADING, filer.NEEDS_REVIEW) and the review shortlist's sentences from tracker/review.py. Imports downwards only - ledger, manifest, filer, review, page - and only runner and api import it; writing the view is the last thing a pass does. tests/conftest.py draws the page again from the live readers through render_page() after every test and requires the same bytes, with only the clock excluded. Decision 103: this page is where the statuses and the Validation Notes are READ: REQUEST_COLUMNS is the manifest's ten plus the four the record holds, side by side, and a keyword a person's filing taught the row is in Any Keywords beside the ones they typed.

### tooling

- **`tools/backtest.py`** — Routes the firm's own already-sorted documents at the office and scores the router against them: the agreement with where a person filed each one, the confusion pairs, the per-row table, the parked and no-text shares, and the time a real pass takes.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.backtest`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 1, `NEUTRAL_STEM` = 'document', `PARKS` = 'parks', `SLOWEST_COUNT` = 10, `HINT_COLUMN` = 'hint', `REPORT_FLAG` = '--report', `EXPECTATIONS_FLAG` = '--expectations', `OUT_FLAG` = '--out', `OCR_FLAG` = '--ocr', `CATALOG_FLAG` = '--catalog', `YEAR_FLAG` = '--year', `REPORT_NOTE` = "How often the router files the firm's own documents where a person already filed them. No file name, no folder name and no word of any document is recorded here.", `BASELINE_NOTE` = "The agreement the firm's own sorted documents scored, measured at the office. No routing change may lower it.", `UNMEASURED_NOTE` = "No backtest has been run against the firm's own documents yet, so there is no agreement to hold a routing change to. Run the backtest at the office and record it.", `NO_BASELINE` = 'No agreement is recorded: the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office. There is no baseline to hold this report to, and an unknown baseline is not a passing one.', `NOTHING_ROUTED` = 'This report routed no document at all, so it cannot be held to the recorded baseline.', `BELOW_BASELINE` = 'Agreement is BELOW the baseline: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `AT_BASELINE` = 'Agreement holds: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `RECORDED` = 'Recorded {agreement} over {documents} document(s) in {path}.'
  - imports: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/settings.py`, `tracker/templates.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
  - imports at call time: `tests/test_real_corpus.py`
  - writes: `docs/backtest-baseline.json`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_backtest.py`
  - note: Decision 74. The measure the fifty blank IRS forms and the typed cases cannot be - decision 70's report leaves most keywords and most rows defended by nothing - and the only corpus made of documents a client actually sent. Each document is routed through a hard link (a copy where the file system refuses one) under one neutral name, so the router's by-name fallback can never read the client's name off the file and the score is the routing rules' rather than the firm's naming discipline; the link is the same bytes, so every tier-2 check still sees the real document. A document with no text layer is its own category, because the only evidence left for it would be the name being hidden - unless OCR is allowed, when nothing is handed over and the router does its own reading under its own stricter rule for OCR words. Catalogs are built the way tests/test_irs_forms.py builds them, with the size floor and the year check lifted. Nothing identifying comes back: counts, catalog identifiers and a row's number in the expectations file, never a file name, a folder name below the corpus root or a word of a document; the corpus, its expectations file and the report stay outside the repository and the tool refuses to write into the tree.
- **`tools/learned_keywords.py`** — Lists what the staff taught the router: every keyword a person taught one engagement's request that no catalog row with the same identifier and document carries, across every engagement under the clients root, grouped by request row with the number of engagements that typed it.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.learned_keywords`
  - constants: `FLAG_INACTIVE` = 'inactive', `CARRIED_BY` = '{n} engagement(s)', `MISFILE` = 'would misfile: {form} {placement}', `FILES_AS` = 'files as {identifier} in the {catalog} catalog', `PARKS` = 'parks in the {catalog} catalog', `SAID_BY` = 'said by: {forms}', `CUSTOM_ROW` = 'no catalog holds this row', `IN_CATALOGS` = 'in the {catalogs} catalog(s)', `NONE` = '- none'
  - imports: `tools/vocab_report.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/settings.py`
  - run by: `automation.manifest.json`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_learned_keywords.py`
  - note: Decision 79. A keyword a filing teaches lives in that one engagement's record, so fifty engagements hold fifty private vocabularies and the catalog is the only one tests/test_catalog.py and tests/test_irs_forms.py defend; this is the season's list of candidates to promote. Read-only in the strong sense: no lock is taken, nothing in an engagement folder is written or moved, and a report path inside the repository is refused - an engagement folder name is a client's name and the report names them on request. The engagement's details have recorded the catalog form since decision 86, but this tool does not read it: a row is compared against every catalog holding it and the report says which matched; a row no catalog holds is a custom request, listed apart with all its keywords. An engagement whose record could not be read is a problem line, never a silent skip. It borrows shipped_catalogs() and corpus_documents() from tools/vocab_report.py, so the catalogs it compares against - built through manifest.validated() over template_items() since decision 104 - and the corpus a candidate can be run over are the coverage report's. manifest_rows() reads through manifest.load_manifest(), which is what puts a taught keyword in front of any reader at all.
- **`tools/repo_map.py`** — Builds and incrementally updates this map. Derives imports, exports, CLIs, test coverage and hashes from source; merges the curated layer on top.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.repo_map`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 2, `MAP_INTRO` = 'Read this instead of re-scanning the repository.', `TESTED_BY` = 'tested by', `EXERCISED_BY` = 'exercised by', `NO_TEST_FILE` = 'no dedicated test file', `IMPORTS_AT_CALL` = 'imports at call time', `REQUIREMENTS_FILES` = ('requirements.txt', 'requirements-build.txt'), `NODE_PREFIXES` = ('artifact:', 'rule:')
  - reads: `docs/repo-map.curated.json`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_repo_map.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Standard library only. `update` re-parses only files whose SHA-256 changed, and a change to this file forces a full rebuild — new derivation rules must not leave edges typed by the old ones. Test edges are three-way on purpose: `tests` (the test file owning the module by name) is coverage, `exercises` (any other test importing it) is not, and a test importing another test is a plain `imports`.
- **`tools/vocab_report.py`** — Generates the vocabulary coverage report: which keyword in each catalog is reached by which IRS form in tests/irs/ or case in tests/test_catalog.py, tested with content_check.says() the way the router reads, and which keywords nothing in the suite defends.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.vocab_report`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 1, `GENERATED_NOTE` = 'GENERATED by tools/vocab_report.py — do not edit by hand.', `INPUT_PATHS` = ('tracker/templates.py', 'tracker/content_check.py', 'tracker/manifest.py', 'tests/test_catalog.py', 'tests/test_irs_forms.py', 'tests/test_real_corpus.py', 'tools/vocab_report.py')
  - imports: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/settings.py`, `tracker/templates.py`
  - used by: `tools/learned_keywords.py`
  - imports at call time: `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`
  - writes: `docs/vocab-coverage.json`, `docs/vocab-coverage.md`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`
  - tested by: `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - note: The map's counterpart for the routing rules (decision 70). `build` extracts the corpus and routes every keyword (about thirty seconds); `check` compares the SHA-256 of its inputs - the catalog, the matcher, the manifest's validation, the cases, the corpus, tests/test_real_corpus.py and this file - so it costs nothing and CI runs it. The committed report reads no client document: the corpus is the IRS's own blank forms and text the suite typed. Decision 71: when TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names the firm's own redacted documents, `build` reads those too (kind `real`) and the counts name them; that report is a local reading, never the committed one, and `check` refuses a committed report that names them. Decision 73: the workbook cases are read too - as_a_sheet() renders a client spreadsheet's rows the way content_check._extract_xlsx does, so a keyword only a schedule reaches is not reported as unreached. Decision 104: shipped_catalogs() builds each catalog through manifest.validated() over template_items(), the same validation an engagement's create makes, with no temporary file and no store - which is why tracker/manifest.py is one of its inputs and the report was rebuilt with this decision at the same numbers.

### ci

- **`.github/workflows/build.yml`** — Builds the portable package on demand (workflow_dispatch or a `v*` tag) by running Build App.bat itself on a Windows runner, proves the frozen executable answers in both of its modes, prints the build-info file and uploads the package as the run's artifact for seven days.
  - runs: `Build App.bat`, `api_entry.py`, `tests/samples.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_build.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It runs the batch file rather than re-implementing the build, because a second copy of the build is the one that drifts; tests/test_build.py refuses a workflow that names PyInstaller, the packager or the copy itself. The batch file pauses for a person at every exit, so it reads one documented switch that skips the waits, named in its own header and set here. The two smoke checks run the frozen executable, not the source: `list` with the shell's two environment variables set, which must answer JSON rather than a traceback on an install with no clients root yet, and one dry pass over a scratch clients root tests/samples.py builds, which walks filing, routing, scanning and drafting. Where the package landed is read back out of the batch file's own OUT/PLATFORM/ARCH and app/package.json's two names, so no path here is a second copy of one. Not on push: a freeze, an npm install, an Electron download and a few hundred megabytes of artifact are not what a commit should cost.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — CI: runs the test suite, `repo_map.py check`, the vocabulary check, the linter and `node --check` on the three Electron files, on Linux and Windows and on two interpreters, on every push to main and every pull request.
  - reads: `requirements.txt`
  - runs: `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: The map check is the point. docs/repo-map.md is what agents read instead of re-scanning, its freshness is guarded by test_the_committed_map_is_current, and this workflow is what makes that guard run without anyone remembering to. Every step always reports, so a stale map and a failing test surface in the same run. Windows is in the matrix because the firm's machine is Windows and the held lock, the atomic replace and the Windows-only tests behave differently there; the python-version line is pinned to pyproject's floor by a guard. Decision 78: the matrix carries the interpreter the office runs beside that floor, because the package is frozen on the office's Python and a suite that has never run there proves nothing about it; the four rows are written out one at a time rather than crossed so the floor stays one readable literal for the guard that pins it.

### desktop-app

- **`app/main.js`** — Electron main process. Spawns the Python API (`python -m tracker.api`, or the frozen executable package.json's config.apiName names in the portable build) and relays its JSON to the renderer over IPC.
  - imports: `app/package.json`
  - spawns: `api_entry.py`, `tracker/api.py`
  - launched by: `Start App.bat`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: This is the cross-language boundary: everything the UI can do is a tracker.api command. The renderer is untrusted here: a command must be in vocab.commands (before the vocabulary arrives, only BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND, pinned to tracker.api.COMMANDS by a guard) with the one argument shape the renderer uses; open-path opens only a path the API reported in state.paths; the tracker's exit code is read, not discarded, and a tracker that outlives TRACKER_TIMEOUT_MS is killed and reported. The window is sandboxed, cannot navigate and cannot open windows.
- **`app/package-lock.json`**
- **`app/package.json`**
  - used by: `app/main.js`
- **`app/preload.js`** — Context bridge exposing only the calls tests/test_single_source.py checks against main.js.call(args, payload), tracker.open(path) and tracker.pickFolder(). Nothing else crosses.
  - called by: `app/renderer/app.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
- **`app/renderer/app.js`** — The desktop UI: the form-type wizard, the request list and the scan results, and (decision 104) the request-list editor - the only place a rule is entered. Talks only to window.tracker from the preload bridge.
  - loaded by: `app/renderer/index.html`
  - calls: `app/preload.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: Every node is built with el() and placed with replaceChildren; there is no innerHTML and no escaper, so a client's file name, a keyword somebody typed into the request list or a folder name is text whatever characters it carries (a guard checks the sinks are absent). Every word it shows or compares comes from the API's vocabulary (applyVocabulary); SCAN_LABEL is the one label it owns. Decision 76: the Needs Review card asks one question of a parked and a set-aside document alike - which request does this belong to - so reviewRow() builds both, and only an open question carries the note box and the button that sets one aside; what a person has set aside is folded under its own count, never removed from the page, because the list is the only way back. Decision 77: renderUnfileList() is the same list for what is already filed - folded away, there for the one row that is wrong - and the function cannot be called after the decision it shows, because the guard on the renderer's vocabulary forbids that word anywhere in the file. Decision 84: the Needs Review card shows the shortlist. renderReview() maps state.review by pbc_location and hands each parked row its triage; reviewRow() puts the shortlist at the head of the picker under the 'suggested' heading, every other request under 'other_requests', and lists the sentence behind each suggestion beneath the row - an <option> carries no second line, and the reason is what is read before anything is picked. The picker starts on the best suggestion, falling back to the router's own first candidate. A parked file the evidence says nothing about shows the vocabulary's nothing_suggested rather than a guess, and a set-aside row is not triaged at all, so it gets no shortlist. Every word of it - the two headings and the File it label as well - comes from vocab; the renderer still types none. Decision 89: a chip beside the engagement's name says whether its own page still describes it. The word and the label are the API's (vocab.view), the chip's class is derived from the word the same way a status chip's is, and the button opens state.paths.view through the same whitelisted opener the Open Status button uses. Decision 91: that button's label is the API's too - applyVocabulary() fills #view-label from vocab.view.open, exactly as it fills the scan button - so the page carries no word for it, and the path it opens is now an .html file the shell hands to the default browser. Decision 104: requestRows() is the one row component - a table of inputs built from vocab.columns (each column's key, header and help; the two numbers as number inputs whose minimum comes from vocab.editor.minimums, the override a pick of vocab.overrides), used by the wizard's custom-request section (three columns, identifiers assigned as rows are added) and by the editor (all ten). openEditor() opens on state.rules - the person's rows as stored, a derived date pattern shown blank, the file types shown as '*' when any - with the engagement's details laid out from vocab.editor.engagement_fields (a text box, a date or a yes/no box for the editable ones, plain text for the rest) and the keywords filings taught shown beside each row as taught (vocab.editor.learned_note), never as typed. pasteRows() appends rows pasted from a spreadsheet by position - tab-separated if any line holds a tab, otherwise CSV through a small RFC 4180 reader, a first line that repeats the headings skipped - and records nothing. saveEditor() is one edit call: a refusal is shown inside the editor with its row and column and the modal stays open; a save renders the state the API returns, closes, and says what changed or that nothing did, with the warnings under vocab.editor.warnings_heading. Every heading, label, hint and button of the editor is vocab.editor's or vocab.columns'; the Check Manifest button and the button that opened the workbook are gone with the workbook.
- **`app/renderer/index.html`** — Desktop app shell markup: empty placeholders the renderer fills from the API's vocabulary, under a Content-Security-Policy that allows nothing but the app's own files. Since decision 104 it holds the request-list editor's modal (#editor), every label of which the renderer fills, and the Edit Request List button (#btn-edit) that opens it; the min of a number input is never typed here.
  - loads: `app/renderer/app.js`, `app/renderer/style.css`
- **`app/renderer/logo.svg`**
- **`app/renderer/style.css`** — Desktop app styling.
  - loaded by: `app/renderer/index.html`

### root

- **`Build App.bat`** — Builds the portable package: freezes the API with PyInstaller from the committed api_entry.spec inside a virtual environment holding exactly requirements-build.txt, packages the Electron shell with @electron/packager, copies the frozen API into resources/ and writes BUILD-INFO.txt.
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - freezes: `api_entry.py`
  - note: Reproducible from the commit (decision 46): the freeze runs in its own venv because PyInstaller follows optional imports and the machine's Python would otherwise leak unrelated packages into the package (decision 53). The packager runs through its entry script under `node`, not the `npx` shim, for the ampersand reason Start App.bat states; the copy into the package is `robocopy` with its exit code checked and the executable's presence asserted, because `xcopy` gave up on the package's long paths while the script still reported success (decision 53). Guards pin OUT to .gitignore and the resources path to app/main.js. Decision 55: the venv is made fresh each build; no parenthesised value is expanded inside the build-info block. Decision 78: every exit goes through one `:wait` label, which pauses for the person who double-clicked unless TRACKER_BUILD_NONINTERACTIVE is set - the one switch, named in this file's header and read nowhere else, and what lets .github/workflows/build.yml run this file rather than a copy of it.
- **`Start App.bat`** — Runs the desktop app from source: checks for Python and Node, installs the Electron packages app/package-lock.json pins (`npm ci`, first run only) and starts Electron.
  - launches: `app/main.js`
  - note: Electron is started through its own entry script under `node`, never the `npx` shim: the shim breaks when the folder's path contains an ampersand, which the firm's own checkout does (decision 53). Electron downloads its binary on the first start, so the install step needs the network once. Decision 55: installs requirements.txt every start (a second when satisfied).
- **`api_entry.py`** — PyInstaller entry point: the portable app's one executable, which is the tracker API by default and the scheduled job (tracker.runner.main) when RUNNER_MODE_FLAG comes first.
  - CLI: `python api_entry.py`
  - imports: `tracker/runner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/api.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - spawned by: `app/main.js`
  - scheduled by: `tracker/scheduling.py`
  - frozen by: `Build App.bat`
  - tested by: `tests/test_api_entry.py`
  - note: PyInstaller needs a real script, not a -m module. Runner mode is dispatched before tracker.api is imported, because the API imports tracker.scheduling whose TASK_NAME needs the product name the Electron shell passes in the environment - and Task Scheduler passes nothing; the job needs neither of the shell's variables. api_entry.spec (committed; reads config.apiName from app/package.json) is how it is frozen.
- **`automation.manifest.json`** — The firm's Command Center integration surface, and the whole of it: the card this tool shows on the office dashboard, and the four actions it offers there - a preview pass, a real pass, the engagement list and the learned keywords. No tracker code reads this file; the Command Center discovers it under its configured roots and runs the argv arrays in it with cwd set to the repository root.
  - runs: `tools/learned_keywords.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
  - note: Decision 81. The Center's safety contract refuses any manifest declaring that it schedules itself, and refusing one never stopped a Task Scheduler entry - it only meant this tool stayed off the board or declared a falsehood. The owner's written exception of 2026-09-18 is declared here in safety.scheduled_exception, the dated field the contract gained the same day, and the card prints that sentence; auto_send and money_movement admit no exception, ever. Each action is an argv array, never a shell string, and every flag it names has to exist in the module it calls. The pass takes the clients root as a positional argument rather than reading settings.py, because Task Scheduler and the Center hand the process none of the shell's environment - api_entry.py's rule: the job needs nothing but its command line; tools/learned_keywords.py takes no parameter here and reads the root from the settings file itself. run-pass carries the log flag ahead of a bare -- so the root that follows is read as the positional and not swallowed as the log's optional value.
- **`conftest.py`** — Puts the repo root on sys.path so tests can `import tracker` without installing the package - explicitly now, beside pyproject's pythonpath, for editor runners and pytest's rootdir detection.
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**

## Tests, documents and data files with a stated purpose

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Agent entry point. Says to read the map instead of re-scanning, how to keep it current, and the standing rules that hold across every module.
  - documents: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/learned_keywords.py`, `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Points at docs/repo-map.md as the first thing to read in a session.
- **`README.md`** — What the system is, how to run each stage, and how to set it up. Who does what is docs/workflow.md.
  - documents: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md`** — The build plan, the hard constraints and the decision log. Every component, all built and tested.
  - documents: `tracker/__init__.py`
  - note: The decision log is the record of WHY: read it before changing behaviour that looks arbitrary.
- **`docs/backtest-baseline.json`** — The one number the backtest commits: how often the router filed the firm's own sorted documents where a person filed them, the count it was measured over, and the day it was measured.
  - written by: `tools/backtest.py`
  - note: Decision 74. Owned by tools/backtest.py; `record` writes it and `check` fails a report below it. It ships with no agreement recorded, and `check` then says plainly that the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office and exits 0 - an unknown baseline is never reported as a met one. It holds a number and a date and nothing a client could be read out of.
- **`docs/repo-map.curated.json`** — The hand-written half of this map: roles, notes, artifacts, cross-language hops and the standing rules. Merged on top of the derived facts and never overwritten by a rebuild.
  - read by: `tools/repo_map.py`
  - note: Edit this, then run `python tools/repo_map.py update`. The generated docs/repo-map.json and docs/repo-map.md are NOT edited by hand.
- **`docs/runbook.md`** — The operator's page for one tax season: the designated machine and why only one may run a clients root, what a person does each morning and on the draft day, what every index reason and validation note means, and the thirty-minute move to another machine.
  - note: Written for a person, not an agent. Roles are docs/workflow.md and the reasons behind the rules are docs/ROADMAP.md; it links to both rather than repeating them.
- **`docs/storage.md`** — The storage plan in prose: the three words (the record, the ledger, the store) and what each means, why the journal syncs with the engagement folder and the database does not, the journal-then-apply order, the schema table, the edit as the event the rules travel in, rebuild as recovery, the check as the gate, what each of the four stages took away, and (decision 107) why the verdict cache is in the store and not in the record.
  - documents: `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - note: Written with decision 101 and finished with 104. It is the page to read before touching storage. The migrations of decisions 102 and 103, which it described step by step, are gone from the tree and from this page; the History section says they existed and where their reading copy is.
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.json`** — The coverage report as data, with the SHA-256 of every input it was built from; `check` and the suite compare against these. Generated; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.md`** — The vocabulary coverage report as people read it: the unreached keywords, the keywords reached only by documents that file elsewhere, the rows nothing files into, then every catalog row by row. Generated by tools/vocab_report.py; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Rebuilt with `python tools/vocab_report.py build` in the same commit as a catalog, matcher or case change.
- **`docs/workflow.md`** — How the day-to-day workflow runs.
- **`requirements-build.txt`** — What Build App.bat installs: requirements.txt plus the pinned PyInstaller.
- **`requirements.txt`** — Runtime and dev dependencies, pinned exactly (a guard refuses a range); the optional OCR extras are documented here too.
  - read by: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  - note: requirements-build.txt adds the pinned freezer on top for Build App.bat; api_entry.spec is the committed freeze and app/package-lock.json the committed Electron install, so a build is made from the commit rather than from whatever was current that day (decision 46).
- **`tests/samples.py`** — The pile of client documents the suite starts from, built from nothing: text_pdf() prints lines to a real one-page PDF, sheet_xlsx() writes rows to a real workbook, and build_samples() assembles the drop folder a client would leave (a duplicate, last year's form, a Word file, a Google Sheets shortcut, a photo, a half-uploaded temp file).
  - used by: `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - note: No fixture files in the repository and no client data, so every test starts from the same pile. It was the marketing demo's sample builder in tracker/api.py; the demo went (decision 41) and the suite still needed the pile. listing_denied() makes a folder really unlistable for the running account, because rglob and os.walk reach the file system by different calls and a monkeypatch of one proves nothing about the other. Decision 73: sheet_xlsx() is how tests/test_catalog.py routes its workbook cases - half of every catalog asks for a schedule a client keeps in Excel, and a sheet is read as rows of tab-separated cells (a phrase across two cells is one phrase, a phrase down two rows is two labels), so typing one as prose would prove the wrong reading. Decision 78: build_scratch_root() assembles the same pile into a whole clients root - one scaffolded engagement with the documents already dropped - which is what .github/workflows/build.yml runs the frozen package over; the fixture lives beside the pile rather than in a tool of its own so there is one pile and not two that drift. It records the engagement through manifest.create_engagement() directly rather than through the suite's helper, because the build workflow imports this module without conftest (decision 104). openpyxl is imported here to WRITE a client's spreadsheet for the suite to read, which is the one use of it the tree keeps.
- **`tests/test_backtest.py`** — Guards the backtest: a document is routed by its text and never by its name, a file with no text layer is counted apart rather than parked, the report and the console carry no file or folder name, the skeleton is blank with the request folder as the hint and is never overwritten, and an unrecorded baseline is said rather than passed.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 74. The corpus it scores is built with tests/samples.py in a temporary folder, because no client document is in the repository or ever will be. It also pins the two things the hiding rests on: the neutral name reaches no keyword in any shipped catalog, and a whole pass writes nothing under the repository root.
- **`tests/test_build.py`** — Guards what only the build workflow could otherwise discover ten minutes into a release: that it runs the batch file the repository owns rather than a copy of the build, that the switch it sets is the one that batch file reads, that the flags it fires at the frozen executable are flags tracker/runner.py declares, that it passes the two environment variables tracker/settings.py names, and that both workflows quote the one interpreter pyproject.toml writes down.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It also asserts the fixture: a scratch root is one engagement discovery finds and a whole dry pass walks, because a smoke check over an empty folder proves only that discovery does not crash. Nothing here can prove the package runs - only the Windows runner can.
- **`tests/test_learned_keywords.py`** — Guards the learned-keyword report: two engagements that taught one keyword are one row with a count of two, a keyword the catalog already carries is not reported, a hand-added row is a custom row, an unreadable record is a problem line, the default output holds no folder name, nothing under the repository is written and a path inside it is refused, and a keyword an IRS form says is marked as one that would misfile it.
  - imports: `tests/conftest.py`
  - note: Decision 79. The clients roots are scratch trees under tmp_path, built the way tests/test_registry.py builds one: tests/conftest.py's make_engagement() records the shipped catalog through create_engagement() and a keyword_learned event teaches the keyword, so what the report compares is a real record rather than a stand-in. The corpus case reads the fifty IRS forms and takes about half a minute.
- **`tests/test_real_corpus.py`** — The harness for the firm's own redacted documents: every row of the expectations file beside them routed against a shipped catalog the way tests/test_irs_forms.py routes the IRS's forms, and asserted to file where the firm says or to park.
  - imports: `tests/test_scanner.py`
  - used by: `tests/test_catalog.py`
  - used at call time by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Decision 71. The corpus is outside the repository, in the folder TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names, and is never committed; with no corpus the routing case skips by name and the harness's own tests - the reading, the routing and the skip - still run on a scratch folder, so the file is exercised on every machine. It owns read_expectations() and real_corpus(), which tools/vocab_report.py imports, so the report and the test cannot disagree about what an expectation means. Decision 74: read_expectations() takes the file's path rather than its folder, because tools/backtest.py scores an expectations file a person keeps wherever they keep it and the contract has to have one reader.
- **`tests/test_repo_map.py`** — Guards the map's trust contract: derived facts come from source, curated judgment survives regeneration, drift is detected, and the committed map matches the tree.
  - note: test_the_committed_map_is_current fails the suite if someone changed code without running `repo_map.py update`.
- **`tests/test_vocab_report.py`** — Guards the coverage report: reach is says(), not a substring; the four headline lists are computed as claimed on small catalogs; the committed report matches its inputs by hash.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`
  - note: test_the_committed_report_is_current fails the suite if a keyword, a case or the matcher changed without `python tools/vocab_report.py build`. Decision 73: a workbook case must read the same to the report as to the suite, so the rendering and a real round trip through openpyxl are asserted equal.

## Artifacts (files the system reads and writes at runtime)

- **`artifact:Prepared/`** — The firm-side working set: renamed copies sorted per request, plus 00 - Needs Review for anything that could not be identified. The client never sees this.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
- **`artifact:Shared/`** — The client's one drop folder — the only thing they see and the only thing they touch. Their originals end up in Shared/PBC/, still visible to them, untouched.
  - written by: `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:Status Report.html`** — The page a person opens (decisions 89 and 91), in the engagement folder beside the record, and the only file there without a leading underscore because it is the one staff are meant to open. One self-contained HTML file - inline style, no image, no font, nothing fetched - with a sticky navigation and four sections: Summary (the record's head, when it was drawn in UTC and in local time, the counts, and the sentence that says it holds no facts of its own), Requests (statuses as coloured badges; since decision 116 the rows set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE are not in the table but folded below it in one page.details() block per year, headed NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION with the label and the count, dimmed, in the same columns - and Override Reason is a column), Index and Needs Review (the parked rows, each with the shortlist review.triage() computes and one line per set-aside row it names). Every table sorts on a click through a few lines of inline script and is a plain table without it. REGENERATED BY EVERY REAL PASS from the readers, never on a dry run. It HOLDS NO FACT - every value on it is the record's - so no fact is read back (read_stamp() reads only the stamp) and there is nothing on it to edit. The stamp is in meta tags in the head (tracker-record-sha256, tracker-generated and one per Summary field), which view_state() reads with a regular expression; since decision 104 the stamp is the record's head alone, because a rules edit is an event and moves it. A page whose replace does not land - on Windows an open read handle is enough to refuse it - is simply not replaced: the run reports view_stale and succeeds, and the one on disk stays honestly behind. The app says current / behind / unknown beside the engagement's name (tracker.view.view_state) and opens it with the Open Status Report button; `python -m tracker.view <folder>` redraws one.
  - written by: `tracker/view.py`
  - read by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/view.py`
- **`artifact:_ledger.jsonl`** — The engagement's own append-only record (decision 87), in the engagement folder beside the client's files: one JSON event per line, in the order the writers wrote them - what was preserved, filed, parked, called a duplicate, decided by a person, had its bytes recorded, taught a keyword, the statuses each scan applied, and (decision 104) the request list and the engagement's details as the app's editor saved them, one rules_changed event per save carrying exactly what moved. Written only under the engagement lock, with O_APPEND and fsync, one line per event and never rewritten; a torn last line is ignored by the reader and truncated by the next append. Since decision 102 it is the whole of the index, since 103 the whole of the statuses, and since 104 the whole of the person's rules: filer.read_index(), manifest.load_manifest() and manifest.load_engagement_info() all answer from the fold of these lines (through the store, which keeps the fold so no reader pays for it twice), and there is no other copy. Its presence is what makes a folder an engagement (tracker/registry.py). A journal from before decision 104 may carry rules_imported and migrated lines; both are folded and neither is ever written again. A record that does not read as one is refused by name and the line, for every reader. A person never edits it, and `python -m tracker.store <store> check <root>` is how a person checks the database against it.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/store.py`, `tracker/view.py`
- **`artifact:reminder-draft.txt`** — The drafted chase email, waiting for a person to read, edit and send. Carries a fingerprint so the weekly job can tell whether it has been edited.
  - written by: `tracker/reminder.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`
- **`artifact:runs.log`** — The one run log in the clients root (LOG_FILENAME in tracker/runner.py): one summary line per pass, appended by a pass run with the log flag - the scheduled task and the Command Center's run-pass action both pass it - never on a dry run, and never read by the system; a person opens it. *(write-only by design: nothing reads it back)*
  - written by: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`artifact:status.html`** — The practice on one page, in the clients root beside the run log: every engagement with what it owes, the review queue across all of them newest first, and everything that failed. Written by every real pass (STATUS_PAGE_FILENAME in tracker/runner.py) and by the app's own pass; read by a person, who opens it from the clients folder or with the app's Open Status button. One self-contained file - no script, nothing fetched - because it names client files. Never on a dry run. *(write-only by design: nothing reads it back)*
  - written by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
- **`artifact:tracker.db`** — The store (decision 101): one SQLite file per clients root, on the designated machine's local disk beside the settings file, holding every engagement's requests, statuses, learned keywords, index rows, details and journal events under that root - all folded from each engagement's journal and from nothing else - and, since decision 107, the tier-3 verdict cache (the verdicts and the file memos), which is the one thing in it that is not a derivation of the journal: a rebuild leaves it empty and the next pass reads each document once. NEVER under the clients root and never in an engagement folder - those sync, and a synced database file is a corrupted database file. Written by tracker/store.py, and through it by the filer, the scanner and the manifest's two writes; read, through the store, by every reader of the index, the request list and the details. Disposable all the same - delete it and every fact it held is still in the journals - so it is never backed up, never synced and a person never opens it. One connection per process (connect(), close()), to the file beside the settings file unless TRACKER_STORE names another; the suite sets that per test. At user_version 3 since decision 107 (2 since 104, when the workbook's digest column went); a file at any other version is refused by name rather than opened, and a version-1 or version-2 file is deleted and rebuilt.
  - written by: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - read by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/review.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`, `tracker/store.py`, `tracker/view.py`

## Rules that cut across the code

- **rule:no-AI-on-client-documents** — No generative AI ever reads a client financial document. Every routing and status decision comes from deterministic rules in the manifest.
  - enforced in: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-ever-sent** — Nothing is ever sent. The system drafts client emails and stops. There is no SMTP, no mail client and no network call in the reminder or scheduling path.
  - enforced in: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-guessed** — Nothing is guessed. A document is filed only when exactly one request accepts it - or, when one document names several forms as itself, when each of those forms is accepted by exactly one request. Ambiguous, contested and unrecognized files go to 00 - Needs Review for a person - misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/review.py`, `tracker/router.py`
- **rule:originals-are-never-altered** — Originals are never altered. Files are moved byte for byte under their own names into Shared/PBC/; all work happens on copies, and every move is recorded in the record.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`

## External dependencies

Python packages are pinned in the requirements files (a Python package with no pin is an optional import, such as the OCR fallback); the desktop shell's packages are pinned in `app/package.json`.

- `electron` — not pinned by a requirements file; used by `app/main.js`, `app/preload.js`
- `openpyxl` — pinned 3.1.5 (requirements.txt); used by `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`
- `pdfplumber` — pinned 0.11.10 (requirements.txt); used by `tracker/content_check.py`
- `pypdf` — pinned 6.7.4 (requirements.txt); used by `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_validators.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
- `pypdfium2` — not pinned by a requirements file; used by `tracker/content_check.py`
- `pytesseract` — not pinned by a requirements file; used by `tracker/content_check.py`
- `pytest` — pinned 9.1.1 (requirements.txt); used by `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_ledger.py`, `tests/test_locking.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_reasons.py`, `tests/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_reminder.py`, `tests/test_repo_map.py`, `tests/test_review.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_scaffold.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`, `tests/test_scheduling.py`, `tests/test_settings.py`, `tests/test_store.py`, `tests/test_templates.py`, `tests/test_view.py`

## Updating this map

```
python tools/repo_map.py update    # after any code change (incremental)
python tools/repo_map.py check     # verify it matches the working tree
```

Derived facts (imports, exports, CLIs, tests, hashes) are parsed from the source — never hand-edit them. Descriptions, artifacts and cross-language hops are curated in `docs/repo-map.curated.json`; edit that file and re-run `update`.
